name: EU AI Act — Artificial Intelligence Act

chapters.title: Transparency obligations for providers and deployers of certain AI systems
Eu database for high-risk AI systems
Post-market monitoring, information sharing and market surveillance
Delegation of power and committee procedure

articles.title: Subject matter
articles.requirement: Lays down harmonised rules for placing on the market, putting into service, and use of AI systems in the Union, as well as prohibitions and requirements for certain AI practices

articles.title: Scope
articles.requirement: Applies to providers, deployers, importers, distributors, and product manufacturers placing or using AI systems in the Union, regardless of establishment location

articles.title: Definitions
articles.requirement: Defines AI system, provider, deployer, high-risk AI system, general-purpose AI model, biometric identification, emotion recognition, and other key terms

articles.title: AI literacy
articles.requirement: Providers and deployers must ensure sufficient AI literacy among staff and other persons dealing with AI systems on their behalf, considering the context of use

articles.title: Prohibited AI practices
articles.requirement: Prohibits AI systems using subliminal manipulation, exploitation of vulnerabilities, social scoring by public authorities, real-time remote biometric identification in public spaces (with exceptions), emotion recognition in workplace/education, untargeted facial image scraping, and biometric categorisation for sensitive attributes

articles.title: Classification rules for high-risk AI systems
articles.requirement: An AI system is high-risk if it is a safety component of a product under Union harmonisation legislation, or falls within Annex III categories (biometrics, critical infrastructure, education, employment, essential services, law enforcement, migration, justice)

articles.title: Amendments to Annex III
articles.requirement: The Commission may amend Annex III by delegated act to add or modify high-risk AI use cases, considering severity, frequency, reversibility, and extent of harm

articles.title: Compliance with the requirements
articles.requirement: High-risk AI systems must comply with requirements set out in Chapter 2 of Title III, taking into account the generally acknowledged state of the art

articles.title: Risk management system
articles.requirement: A continuous risk management system must be established, implemented, documented, and maintained throughout the high-risk AI system's lifecycle, identifying and mitigating known and foreseeable risks

articles.title: Data and data governance
articles.requirement: Training, validation, and testing datasets must be subject to data governance and management practices covering design choices, data collection, preparation, labelling, bias examination, and gap identification

articles.title: Technical documentation
articles.requirement: Technical documentation must be drawn up before placing on the market and kept up to date, enabling assessment of compliance with requirements in a clear and comprehensive manner

articles.title: Record-keeping
articles.requirement: High-risk AI systems must allow automatic recording of events (logs) throughout the system's lifetime to ensure traceability of functioning, including inputs, outputs, and decision processes

articles.title: Transparency and provision of information to deployers
articles.requirement: High-risk AI systems must be designed to enable deployers to interpret output and use appropriately. Instructions must include provider identity, system characteristics, performance, limitations, and human oversight measures

articles.title: Human oversight
articles.requirement: High-risk AI systems must be designed to allow effective human oversight, including the ability to understand capacities, monitor operation, interpret output, decide not to use the system, and intervene or stop it

articles.title: Accuracy, robustness and cybersecurity
articles.requirement: High-risk AI systems must achieve appropriate levels of accuracy, robustness, and cybersecurity throughout their lifecycle, and be resilient to errors, faults, and attempts at manipulation

articles.title: Obligations of providers of high-risk AI systems
articles.requirement: Providers must ensure compliance, establish quality management, maintain documentation, keep logs, undertake conformity assessment, affix CE marking, register in EU database, and take corrective actions

articles.title: Quality management system
articles.requirement: Providers must establish a quality management system documented in policies and procedures covering regulatory strategy, design, testing, data management, risk management, post-market monitoring, and incident reporting

articles.title: Documentation keeping
articles.requirement: Provider must keep technical documentation, quality management documentation, conformity declarations, and EU database registration information for 10 years after placing on the market

articles.title: Automatically generated logs
articles.requirement: Providers must keep logs automatically generated by high-risk AI systems for a period appropriate to the intended purpose, and at least 6 months unless otherwise provided

articles.title: Corrective actions and duty of information
articles.requirement: Providers who consider their high-risk AI system non-compliant must immediately take corrective action and inform distributors, deployers, and authorised representatives

articles.title: Cooperation with competent authorities
articles.requirement: Providers of high-risk AI systems shall, upon a reasoned request by a competent authority, provide that authority all the information and documentation necessary to demonstrate the conformity of the high-risk AI system with the requirements set out in Section 2, in a language which can be easily understood by the…

articles.title: Authorised representatives of providers of high-risk AI systems
articles.requirement: Providers established outside the Union must appoint an authorised representative established in the Union by written mandate before placing a high-risk AI system on the market

articles.title: Obligations of importers
articles.requirement: Before placing a high-risk AI system on the market, importers shall ensure that the system is in conformity with this Regulation by verifying that: (a) the relevant conformity assessment procedure referred to in Article 43 has been carried out by the provider of the high-risk AI system; (b) the provider has drawn up…

articles.title: Obligations of distributors
articles.requirement: Before making a high-risk AI system available on the market, distributors shall verify that it bears the required CE marking, that it is accompanied by a copy of the EU declaration of conformity referred to in Article 47 and instructions for use, and that the provider and the importer of that system, as applicable,…

articles.title: Responsibilities along the AI value chain
articles.requirement: Any distributor, importer, deployer or other third-party shall be considered to be a provider of a high-risk AI system for the purposes of this Regulation and shall be subject to the obligations of the provider under Article 16, in any of the following circumstances: (a) they put their name or trademark on a high-risk…

articles.title: Obligations of deployers of high-risk AI systems
articles.requirement: Deployers must use high-risk AI systems in accordance with instructions, ensure human oversight by trained persons, monitor operation, keep logs, carry out DPIA where required, and inform affected persons

articles.title: Fundamental rights impact assessment for high-risk AI systems
articles.requirement: Deployers that are bodies governed by public law or private entities providing public services must perform a fundamental rights impact assessment before putting a high-risk AI system into use

articles.title: Notifying authorities
articles.requirement: Each Member State shall designate or establish at least one notifying authority responsible for setting up and carrying out the necessary procedures for the assessment, designation and notification of conformity assessment bodies and for their monitoring.

articles.title: Application of a conformity assessment body for notification
articles.requirement: Conformity assessment bodies shall submit an application for notification to the notifying authority of the Member State in which they are established.

articles.title: Notification procedure
articles.requirement: Notifying authorities may notify only conformity assessment bodies which have satisfied the requirements laid down in Article 31.

articles.title: Requirements relating to notified bodies
articles.requirement: A notified body shall be established under the national law of a Member State and shall have legal personality. Notified bodies shall satisfy the organisational, quality management, resources and process requirements that are necessary to fulfil their tasks, as well as suitable cybersecurity requirements.

articles.title: Presumption of conformity with requirements relating to notified bodies
articles.requirement: Where a conformity assessment body demonstrates its conformity with the criteria laid down in the relevant harmonised standards or parts thereof, the references of which have been published in the Official Journal of the European Union , it shall be presumed to comply with the requirements set out in Article 31 in so…

articles.title: Subsidiaries of notified bodies and subcontracting
articles.requirement: Where a notified body subcontracts specific tasks connected with the conformity assessment or has recourse to a subsidiary, it shall ensure that the subcontractor or the subsidiary meets the requirements laid down in Article 31, and shall inform the notifying authority accordingly.

articles.title: Operational obligations of notified bodies
articles.requirement: Notified bodies shall verify the conformity of high-risk AI systems in accordance with the conformity assessment procedures set out in Article 43.

articles.title: Identification numbers and lists of notified bodies
articles.requirement: The Commission shall assign a single identification number to each notified body, even where a body is notified under more than one Union act.

articles.title: Changes to notifications
articles.requirement: The notifying authority shall notify the Commission and the other Member States of any relevant changes to the notification of a notified body via the electronic notification tool referred to in Article 30(2).

articles.title: Challenge to the competence of notified bodies
articles.requirement: The Commission shall, where necessary, investigate all cases where there are reasons to doubt the competence of a notified body or the continued fulfilment by a notified body of the requirements laid down in Article 31 and of its applicable responsibilities.

articles.title: Coordination of notified bodies
articles.requirement: The Commission shall ensure that, with regard to high-risk AI systems, appropriate coordination and cooperation between notified bodies active in the conformity assessment procedures pursuant to this Regulation are put in place and properly operated in the form of a sectoral group of notified bodies.

articles.title: Conformity assessment bodies of third countries
articles.requirement: Conformity assessment bodies established under the law of a third country with which the Union has concluded an agreement may be authorised to carry out the activities of notified bodies under this Regulation, provided that they meet the requirements laid down in Article 31 or they ensure an equivalent level of…

articles.title: Harmonised standards and standardisation deliverables
articles.requirement: High-risk AI systems or general-purpose AI models which are in conformity with harmonised standards or parts thereof the references of which have been published in the Official Journal of the European Union in accordance with Regulation (EU) No 1025/2012 shall be presumed to be in conformity with the requirements set…

articles.title: Common specifications
articles.requirement: The Commission may adopt, implementing acts establishing common specifications for the requirements set out in Section 2 of this Chapter or, as applicable, for the obligations set out in Sections 2 and 3 of Chapter V where the following conditions have been fulfilled: (a) the Commission has requested, pursuant to…

articles.title: Presumption of conformity with certain requirements
articles.requirement: High-risk AI systems that have been trained and tested on data reflecting the specific geographical, behavioural, contextual or functional setting within which they are intended to be used shall be presumed to comply with the relevant requirements laid down in Article 10(4).

articles.title: Conformity assessment
articles.requirement: Providers of high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III must undergo conformity assessment (internal control or third-party assessment depending on the category) before placing on the market

articles.title: Certificates
articles.requirement: Certificates issued by notified bodies in accordance with Annex VII shall be drawn-up in a language which can be easily understood by the relevant authorities in the Member State in which the notified body is established.

articles.title: Information obligations of notified bodies
articles.requirement: Notified bodies shall inform the notifying authority of the following: (a) any Union technical documentation assessment certificates, any supplements to those certificates, and any quality management system approvals issued in accordance with the requirements of Annex VII; (b) any refusal, restriction, suspension or…

articles.title: Derogation from conformity assessment procedure
articles.requirement: By way of derogation from Article 43 and upon a duly justified request, any market surveillance authority may authorise the placing on the market or the putting into service of specific high-risk AI systems within the territory of the Member State concerned, for exceptional reasons of public security or the protection…

articles.title: EU declaration of conformity
articles.requirement: Provider must draw up a written EU declaration of conformity for each high-risk AI system, keep it for 10 years, and provide a copy to national authorities on request

articles.title: CE marking
articles.requirement: High-risk AI systems must bear the CE marking visibly, legibly, and indelibly, indicating conformity with the Regulation

articles.title: Registration
articles.requirement: Providers and deployers of high-risk AI systems must register themselves and their systems in the EU database before placing on the market or putting into service

articles.title: Transparency obligations for providers and deployers of certain AI systems
articles.requirement: Providers must ensure that AI systems intended to interact with persons, generate synthetic content (deepfakes), or perform emotion recognition or biometric categorisation are marked and disclosed to users

articles.title: Classification of general-purpose AI models as general-purpose AI models with systemic risk
articles.requirement: A GPAI model is classified as having systemic risk if it has high impact capabilities (>10^25 FLOPs cumulative compute) or is designated by Commission decision based on evaluation criteria

articles.title: Procedure
articles.requirement: Where a general-purpose AI model meets the condition referred to in Article 51(1), point (a), the relevant provider shall notify the Commission without delay and in any event within two weeks after that requirement is met or it becomes known that it will be met.

articles.title: Obligations for providers of general-purpose AI models
articles.requirement: Providers must maintain technical documentation, provide information to downstream providers, establish a copyright compliance policy, and publish a sufficiently detailed summary of training content

articles.title: Authorised representatives of providers of general-purpose AI models
articles.requirement: Providers of GPAI models established outside the Union must appoint an authorised representative in the Union before placing a model on the market

articles.title: Obligations of providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risk
articles.requirement: Providers of GPAI models with systemic risk must perform model evaluation, assess and mitigate systemic risks, track and report serious incidents, and ensure adequate cybersecurity protection

articles.title: Codes of practice
articles.requirement: The AI Office facilitates drawing up of codes of practice to contribute to proper application of GPAI model obligations; providers may demonstrate compliance through adherence to codes

articles.title: AI regulatory sandboxes
articles.requirement: Member States must establish at least one AI regulatory sandbox at national level to facilitate development and testing of innovative AI systems under regulatory oversight before placement on the market

articles.title: Detailed arrangements for, and functioning of, AI regulatory sandboxes
articles.requirement: In order to avoid fragmentation across the Union, the Commission shall adopt implementing acts specifying the detailed arrangements for the establishment, development, implementation, operation and supervision of the AI regulatory sandboxes.

articles.title: Further processing of personal data for developing certain AI systems in the public interest in the AI regulatory sandbox
articles.requirement: In the AI regulatory sandbox, personal data lawfully collected for other purposes may be processed solely for the purpose of developing, training and testing certain AI systems in the sandbox when all of the following conditions are met: (a) AI systems shall be developed for safeguarding substantial public interest by…

articles.title: Testing of high-risk AI systems in real world conditions outside AI regulatory sandboxes
articles.requirement: Testing of high-risk AI systems in real world conditions may be permitted outside sandboxes under specific conditions including testing plan, informed consent, and supervisory approval

articles.title: Informed consent to participate in testing in real world conditions outside AI regulatory sandboxes
articles.requirement: For the purpose of testing in real world conditions under Article 60, freely-given informed consent shall be obtained from the subjects of testing prior to their participation in such testing and after their having been duly informed with concise, clear, relevant, and understandable information regarding: (a) the…

articles.title: Measures for providers and deployers, in particular SMEs, including start-ups
articles.requirement: Member States shall undertake the following actions: (a) provide SMEs, including start-ups, having a registered office or a branch in the Union, with priority access to the AI regulatory sandboxes, to the extent that they fulfil the eligibility conditions and selection criteria; the priority access shall not preclude…

articles.title: Derogations for specific operators
articles.requirement: Microenterprises within the meaning of Recommendation 2003/361/EC may comply with certain elements of the quality management system required by Article 17 of this Regulation in a simplified manner, provided that they do not have partner enterprises or linked enterprises within the meaning of that Recommendation.

articles.title: AI Office
articles.requirement: The Commission shall develop Union expertise and capabilities in the field of AI through the AI Office. Member States shall facilitate the tasks entrusted to the AI Office, as reflected in this Regulation.

articles.title: Establishment and structure of the European Artificial Intelligence Board
articles.requirement: A European Artificial Intelligence Board (the ‘Board') is hereby established. The Board shall be composed of one representative per Member State.

articles.title: Tasks of the Board
articles.requirement: The Board shall advise and assist the Commission and the Member States in order to facilitate the consistent and effective application of this Regulation.

articles.title: Advisory forum
articles.requirement: An advisory forum shall be established to provide technical expertise and advise the Board and the Commission, and to contribute to their tasks under this Regulation.

articles.title: Scientific panel of independent experts
articles.requirement: The Commission shall, by means of an implementing act, make provisions on the establishment of a scientific panel of independent experts (the ‘scientific panel') intended to support the enforcement activities under this Regulation.

articles.title: Access to the pool of experts by the Member States
articles.requirement: Member States may call upon experts of the scientific panel to support their enforcement activities under this Regulation. The Member States may be required to pay fees for the advice and support provided by the experts.

articles.title: Designation of national competent authorities and single points of contact
articles.requirement: Each Member State shall establish or designate as national competent authorities at least one notifying authority and at least one market surveillance authority for the purposes of this Regulation.

articles.title: EU database for high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III
articles.theme: Eu database for high-risk AI systems
articles.requirement: The Commission shall, in collaboration with the Member States, set up and maintain an EU database containing information referred to in paragraphs 2 and 3 of this Article concerning high-risk AI systems referred to in Article 6(2) which are registered in accordance with Articles 49 and 60 and AI systems that are not…

articles.title: Post-market monitoring by providers and post-market monitoring plan for high-risk AI systems
articles.theme: Post-market monitoring, information sharing and market surveillance
articles.requirement: Providers shall establish and document a post-market monitoring system in a manner that is proportionate to the nature of the AI technologies and the risks of the high-risk AI system.

articles.title: Reporting of serious incidents
articles.theme: Post-market monitoring, information sharing and market surveillance
articles.requirement: Providers of high-risk AI systems placed on the Union market shall report any serious incident to the market surveillance authorities of the Member States where that incident occurred.

articles.title: Market surveillance and control of AI systems in the Union market
articles.requirement: Market surveillance authorities must carry out market surveillance in accordance with Regulation (EU) 2019/1020. Each Member State must designate a national competent authority

articles.title: Mutual assistance, market surveillance and control of general-purpose AI systems
articles.theme: Post-market monitoring, information sharing and market surveillance
articles.requirement: Where an AI system is based on a general-purpose AI model, and the model and the system are developed by the same provider, the AI Office shall have powers to monitor and supervise compliance of that AI system with obligations under this Regulation.

articles.title: Supervision of testing in real world conditions by market surveillance authorities
articles.theme: Post-market monitoring, information sharing and market surveillance
articles.requirement: Market surveillance authorities shall have competences and powers to ensure that testing in real world conditions is in accordance with this Regulation.

articles.title: Powers of authorities protecting fundamental rights
articles.theme: Post-market monitoring, information sharing and market surveillance
articles.requirement: National public authorities or bodies which supervise or enforce the respect of obligations under Union law protecting fundamental rights, including the right to non-discrimination, in relation to the use of high-risk AI systems referred to in Annex III shall have the power to request and access any documentation…

articles.title: Confidentiality
articles.theme: Post-market monitoring, information sharing and market surveillance
articles.requirement: The Commission, market surveillance authorities and notified bodies and any other natural or legal person involved in the application of this Regulation shall, in accordance with Union or national law, respect the confidentiality of information and data obtained in carrying out their tasks and activities in such a…

articles.title: Procedure at national level for dealing with AI systems presenting a risk
articles.requirement: Where a market surveillance authority finds a high-risk AI system non-compliant or presenting a risk, it must require the provider to take corrective action, withdraw, or recall the system

articles.title: Procedure for dealing with AI systems classified by the provider as non-high-risk in application of Annex III
articles.theme: Post-market monitoring, information sharing and market surveillance
articles.requirement: Where a market surveillance authority has sufficient reason to consider that an AI system classified by the provider as non-high-risk pursuant to Article 6(3) is indeed high-risk, the market surveillance authority shall carry out an evaluation of the AI system concerned in respect of its classification as a high-risk…

articles.title: Union safeguard procedure
articles.theme: Post-market monitoring, information sharing and market surveillance
articles.requirement: Where, within three months of receipt of the notification referred to in Article 79(5), or within 30 days in the case of non-compliance with the prohibition of the AI practices referred to in Article 5, objections are raised by the market surveillance authority of a Member State to a measure taken by another market…

articles.title: Compliant AI systems which present a risk
articles.theme: Post-market monitoring, information sharing and market surveillance
articles.requirement: Where, having performed an evaluation under Article 79, after consulting the relevant national public authority referred to in Article 77(1), the market surveillance authority of a Member State finds that although a high-risk AI system complies with this Regulation, it nevertheless presents a risk to the health or…

articles.title: Formal non-compliance
articles.theme: Post-market monitoring, information sharing and market surveillance
articles.requirement: Where the market surveillance authority of a Member State makes one of the following findings, it shall require the relevant provider to put an end to the non-compliance concerned, within a period it may prescribe: (a) the CE marking has been affixed in violation of Article 48; (b) the CE marking has not been affixed;…

articles.title: Union AI testing support structures
articles.theme: Post-market monitoring, information sharing and market surveillance
articles.requirement: The Commission shall designate one or more Union AI testing support structures to perform the tasks listed under Article 21(6) of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 in the area of AI.

articles.title: Right to lodge a complaint with a market surveillance authority
articles.requirement: Any natural or legal person may lodge a complaint with the relevant market surveillance authority regarding non-compliance with the Regulation

articles.title: Right to explanation of individual decision-making
articles.requirement: Affected persons subject to a decision taken by a deployer on the basis of output from a high-risk AI system have the right to obtain clear and meaningful explanations of the role of the AI system

articles.title: Reporting of infringements and protection of reporting persons
articles.theme: Post-market monitoring, information sharing and market surveillance
articles.requirement: Directive (EU) 2019/1937 shall apply to the reporting of infringements of this Regulation and the protection of persons reporting such infringements.

articles.title: Enforcement of the obligations of providers of general-purpose AI models
articles.theme: Post-market monitoring, information sharing and market surveillance
articles.requirement: The Commission shall have exclusive powers to supervise and enforce Chapter V, taking into account the procedural guarantees under Article 94.

articles.title: Monitoring actions
articles.theme: Post-market monitoring, information sharing and market surveillance
articles.requirement: For the purpose of carrying out the tasks assigned to it under this Section, the AI Office may take the necessary actions to monitor the effective implementation and compliance with this Regulation by providers of general-purpose AI models, including their adherence to approved codes of practice.

articles.title: Alerts of systemic risks by the scientific panel
articles.theme: Post-market monitoring, information sharing and market surveillance
articles.requirement: The scientific panel may provide a qualified alert to the AI Office where it has reason to suspect that: (a) a general-purpose AI model poses concrete identifiable risk at Union level; or (b) a general-purpose AI model meets the conditions referred to in Article 51.

articles.title: Power to request documentation and information
articles.theme: Post-market monitoring, information sharing and market surveillance
articles.requirement: The Commission may request the provider of the general-purpose AI model concerned to provide the documentation drawn up by the provider in accordance with Articles 53 and 55, or any additional information that is necessary for the purpose of assessing compliance of the provider with this Regulation.

articles.title: Power to conduct evaluations
articles.theme: Post-market monitoring, information sharing and market surveillance
articles.requirement: The AI Office, after consulting the Board, may conduct evaluations of the general-purpose AI model concerned: (a) to assess compliance of the provider with obligations under this Regulation, where the information gathered pursuant to Article 91 is insufficient; or (b) to investigate systemic risks at Union level of…

articles.title: Power to request measures
articles.theme: Post-market monitoring, information sharing and market surveillance
articles.requirement: Where necessary and appropriate, the Commission may request providers to: (a) take appropriate measures to comply with the obligations set out in Articles 53 and 54; (b) implement mitigation measures, where the evaluation carried out in accordance with Article 92 has given rise to serious and substantiated concern of…

articles.title: Procedural rights of economic operators of the general-purpose AI model
articles.theme: Post-market monitoring, information sharing and market surveillance
articles.requirement: Article 18 of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020 shall apply mutatis mutandis to the providers of the general-purpose AI model, without prejudice to more specific procedural rights provided for in this Regulation.

articles.title: Codes of conduct for voluntary application of specific requirements
articles.requirement: The AI Office and the Member States shall encourage and facilitate the drawing up of codes of conduct, including related governance mechanisms, intended to foster the voluntary application to AI systems, other than high-risk AI systems, of some or all of the requirements set out in Chapter III, Section 2 taking into…

articles.title: Guidelines from the Commission on the implementation of this Regulation
articles.requirement: The Commission shall develop guidelines on the practical implementation of this Regulation, and in particular on: (a) the application of the requirements and obligations referred to in Articles 8 to 15 and in Article 25; (b) the prohibited practices referred to in Article 5; (c) the practical implementation of the…

articles.title: Exercise of the delegation
articles.theme: Delegation of power and committee procedure
articles.requirement: The power to adopt delegated acts is conferred on the Commission subject to the conditions laid down in this Article.

articles.title: Committee procedure
articles.theme: Delegation of power and committee procedure
articles.requirement: The Commission shall be assisted by a committee. That committee shall be a committee within the meaning of Regulation (EU) No 182/2011. Where reference is made to this paragraph, Article 5 of Regulation (EU) No 182/2011 shall apply.

articles.title: Penalties
articles.requirement: Fines up to EUR 35M/7% global turnover for prohibited AI practices, up to EUR 15M/3% for high-risk system violations, and up to EUR 7.5M/1% for supplying incorrect information

articles.title: Administrative fines on Union institutions, bodies, offices and agencies
articles.requirement: The European Data Protection Supervisor may impose administrative fines on Union institutions, bodies, offices and agencies falling within the scope of this Regulation.

articles.title: Fines for providers of general-purpose AI models
articles.requirement: The Commission may impose on providers of general-purpose AI models fines not exceeding 3 % of their annual total worldwide turnover in the preceding financial year or EUR 15 000 000, whichever is higher., when the Commission finds that the provider intentionally or negligently: (a) infringed the relevant provisions…

articles.requirement: In Article 4(3) of Regulation (EC) No 300/2008, the following subparagraph is added: ‘When adopting detailed measures related to technical specifications and procedures for approval and use of security equipment concerning Artificial Intelligence systems within the meaning of Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 of the European…

articles.requirement: In Article 8 of Directive 2014/90/EU, the following paragraph is added: ‘5.

articles.title: AI systems already placed on the market or put into service and general-purpose AI models already placed on the marked
articles.requirement: Without prejudice to the application of Article 5 as referred to in Article 113(3), point (a), AI systems which are components of the large-scale IT systems established by the legal acts listed in Annex X that have been placed on the market or put into service before 2 August 2027 shall be brought into compliance with…

articles.title: Evaluation and review
articles.requirement: The Commission shall assess the need for amendment of the list set out in Annex III and of the list of prohibited AI practices laid down in Article 5, once a year following the entry into force of this Regulation, and until the end of the period of the delegation of power laid down in Article 97.

articles.title: Entry into force and application
articles.requirement: Enters into force 1 August 2024. Prohibited practices apply from 2 February 2025. GPAI obligations from 2 August 2025. High-risk obligations from 2 August 2026
